name: NiSource Inc.

profile.description: NiSource (Merrillville, IN; roots to 1847) is a regulated natural gas and electric utility operating Columbia Gas distribution (~37,300 miles of main across Ohio, Pennsylvania, Virginia, Kentucky and Maryland) and NIPSCO electric service to ~0.5M customers in northern Indiana [3]. Under CEO Lloyd Yates, its GenCo structure serves large data-center loads: an October 2026 20-year Microsoft agreement adds ~1,100 MW, ~5 GW of GenCo capacity is signed, and a $40B 2027-2033 capital plan targets 10-11% consolidated adjusted EPS CAGR [1]. Q3 2026 GAAP EPS was $0.27 (vs $0.20), and 2026 adjusted EPS guidance was narrowed to the upper half of $2.02-$2.07 [1][2].

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): The GenCo model, which ring-fences generation built for hyperscale customers so existing ratepayers gain ~$1.75B of cost savings, opened a new revenue stream and was extended in October 2026 with a 20-year, ~1,100 MW Microsoft agreement [1]. Coal exit by 2028 with renewables replacement is a second structural shift [5]. AI Deployment (2/2): Management reports its AI work-management intelligence tool delivered field productivity uplifts of over 20%, a quantified internal result [4]. Market Share (1/2): NiSource is a regulated franchise monopoly in its territories; it leads locally but does not define a category [3]. Pipeline (2/2): ~5 GW of signed GenCo capacity, 2 GW under negotiation and up to 2 GW in development, with GenCo EPS contributions guided at $0.05-$0.09 in 2027, $0.32-$0.40 in 2030 and $0.52-$0.68 in 2033 [1]. R&D Intensity (0/1): No meaningful R&D spending is reported [6].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Management's stated focus on safe, reliable and affordable energy, reinforced by structuring GenCo so data-center growth lowers costs for existing customers, is clear but standard for a utility [1][4]. The 2018 Merrimack Valley gas explosions (one death, dozens injured, 100+ homes damaged) remain a reminder that the safety mission has failed before [5]. Community Impact (1/2): NiSource reports community programs and ESG recognition (MSCI AAA) in its ESG reports, plus Merrimack Valley restoration and municipal settlements, but no distinctive dollar-quantified program surfaced [5]. Employee Retention (0/2): No retention or tenure data was found. Insider Buying (0/2): The most recent open-market insider purchase on record is CEO Yates's 40,000 shares at $26.44 in August 2023; none in the last 12 months [6].

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as a Dividend stock (2.68% yield on the $1.20 annual rate, 10+ years of payments) [6]. Full marks on forward P/E of 19.9x (derived from FY2027 consensus EPS of $2.25), 11 consecutive years of dividend growth (2016-2026 on split-adjusted data), 12+ years of payments in the dataset (2x weight) and a 6.4% five-year dividend CAGR ($0.88 to $1.20 annualized; 2x weight) [6]. TTM revenue growth of 10.0% scores ~1.0 and the FY2020-FY2025 revenue CAGR of 7.3% scores 0.82 [6]. Drags: debt-to-equity of 191% (0.47), ROE of 9.8% (0.66), net margin of 13.5% (0.68) and a 60.8% payout ratio (0.65) [6]. Weighted sum 10.27/12 = 8.56, rounded to 9. Liquidity (~$262M daily traded value) easily clears the floor; FMP forward PEG of 2.49 is shown for reference only (not scored for Dividend sleeve).

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): Gas distribution and electric generation are physical, regulated monopoly services that AI cannot displace, and AI is a direct demand driver: ~5 GW of signed GenCo capacity serving hyperscale data centers, including the new 20-year Microsoft agreement [1]. The withheld point reflects that data-center-driven load growth also raises execution and regulatory risk, already visible when federal authorities ordered NIPSCO's Schahfer coal plant kept running 90 days past its December 2025 retirement for grid reliability [5]. AI Opportunity (1/1): GenCo revenue is tied to data-center demand with quantified EPS contributions of $0.05-$0.09 in 2027 rising to $0.52-$0.68 by 2033 [1].

infinite_game.summary: Through Simon Sinek's lens, NiSource is a well-run regulated utility that is beginning to act with a longer horizon: GenCo is designed so that serving data centers lowers costs for ordinary customers, and the company committed to exit coal by 2028. But its public story is still told in EPS CAGR targets and capital-plan dollars, and the Merrimack Valley disaster shows what happens when the operating cause slips, so it sits at the top of the finite range.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): NiSource's emphasis on safe, affordable energy is genuine but not articulated as a vision beyond utility service; investor messaging leads with the 10-11% EPS CAGR and $40B plan [1]. The 2018 Merrimack Valley explosions, which led to a U.S. Senate hearing, show the cause was not resilient under past leadership [5].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Committing to retire 100% of coal by 2028 and designing GenCo so existing customers capture ~$1.75B of savings rather than bearing data-center costs are principled choices with real near-term cost [1][5]. The pattern is still young under Yates.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Management credits a culture of accountability for executing large construction programs, and the AI work-management rollout is framed around empowering field crews [4]. No Glassdoor or retention data surfaced to confirm exceptional trust, so the score is average.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): NiSource is shifting NIPSCO from coal to renewables and gas and adding the GenCo business model for hyperscale load, meaningful adaptation within the regulated-utility framework rather than a reinvention [1][5].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): As a franchise monopoly, NiSource has little competitive language; no management commentary was found referencing peer utilities as examples to learn from [1][4].

investment_thesis: NiSource has become a data-center growth utility: the October 2026 Microsoft agreement brings signed GenCo capacity to ~5 GW, and management raised its 2027-2033 consolidated adjusted EPS CAGR target to 10-11% on a $40B capital plan, with 2027 EPS guided to $2.22-$2.30 [1]. Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $0.27 beat the $0.22 consensus [2]. The stock trades at ~19.9x 2027 consensus EPS with a 2.68% yield, 11 straight years of dividend growth and a 6.4% five-year dividend CAGR, earning a 9/10 Infrastructure score [6].
thesis_continued: The bear case is balance-sheet strain and regulatory risk: debt-to-equity is 191%, free cash flow is deeply negative (capex is ~166% of operating cash flow), and the $40B plan will require heavy external financing [6]. Analysts note no update on Indiana's review of utility allowed returns, data-center contracts concentrate risk in a few hyperscalers, and coal retirements are already being delayed by federal reliability orders [2][5]. Weak Inspiration (3/10) and a FINITE Infinite Game score (4/10) cap the overall at 64, a HOLD.
key_catalysts: GenCo execution: converting the ~2 GW under strategic negotiation into signed contracts and delivering the guided $0.05-$0.09 EPS contribution in 2027 [1]
2027 adjusted EPS guidance of $2.22-$2.30 and the 6-8% base-plan growth extended through 2033 [1]
Indiana regulatory decisions on allowed returns and GenCo cost allocation protecting customer affordability [2]
key_risks: Financing burden: a $40B capital plan against negative free cash flow and 191% debt-to-equity implies sustained debt and equity issuance [1][6]
Hyperscaler concentration: GenCo economics depend on long-term contracts with a small number of data-center customers such as Microsoft [1]
Regulatory and reliability risk, including federal orders delaying the Schahfer coal plant retirement and possible changes to Indiana utility profit rates [5][2]
